rounds.proof_sketch: Race condition exists in CUDA kernel, but forward() compares custom_result vs torch_result with rtol=atol=1e-4. If race causes error >1e-4, fallback to correct PyTorch result. If race causes error ≤1e-4, error is below our test threshold of 1e-2. In all cases, output difference from reference ≤ max(1e-4, test threshold) cannot exceed kill threshold.
rounds.survival_reason: The forward() function implements a self-correcting validation mechanism that compares the custom CUDA kernel output against PyTorch's matmul. When errors exceed rtol=atol=1e-4 (which would happen if the race condition produced significant wrong values), the function falls back to returning PyTorch's correct result. Since our kill threshold is rtol=atol=1e-2, any error large enough to potentially kill the mutant gets auto-corrected by the fallback. Smaller errors pass the internal validation and are also below our detection threshold. Thread scheduling (which determines if the race triggers) is independent of input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under value-variation testing. The race condition's manifestation depends on hardware thread scheduling, not input values. Even if the race triggers, the forward() function's fallback mechanism (comparing against torch.matmul with rtol=atol=1e-4) auto-corrects any significant errors before the output is returned. To kill this mutant would require either: (1) modifying the forward() function to remove the fallback, or (2) changing the internal validation threshold to be looser than 1e-2.
rounds.recommendations: Self-correcting validation logic in model forward() methods can inadvertently mask kernel bugs during mutation testing. Consider separating validation/debugging code from production code paths, or ensure test frameworks bypass such defensive mechanisms when testing kernel correctness directly.
